name: Jesse Arreguín
title: California State Senator, Chair of the Senate Housing Committee and Chair of the Senate Public Safety Committee
district: California State Senate District 7 (Alameda, Albany, Berkeley, El Cerrito, Emeryville, Hercules, Oakland, Piedmont, Pinole, Richmond, and San Pablo, plus a portion of San Francisco), per official Senate district description at sd07.senate.ca.gov.
years_of_service: Sworn in December 3, 2024; current term. Elected November 5, 2024, succeeding termed-out Sen. Nancy Skinner in this Berkeley/Oakland/Richmond-area seat. (Note: Wikipedia's infobox also lists Steve Glazer, who held the pre-2021-redistricting SD7 number representing a different, Contra Costa-based district, as a 'predecessor'; that reflects district-number continuity rather than a shared constituency. The seat Arreguín won is the seat previously represented by Skinner.)
background: Arreguín was born September 4, 1984 in Fresno, California, and raised in San Francisco by parents and grandparents who worked as migrant farmworkers; he was the first in his family to attend college. He earned a B.A. in Political Science from the University of California, Berkeley. (Source: Wikipedia biography, used here because Ballotpedia's page for Arreguín could not be retrieved, see note in sources below; corroborated in general terms by the official Senate biography at sd07.senate.ca.gov, which states he was 'born in Fresno and raised in San Francisco by parents who were migrant farm workers.')

Before elected office, Arreguín worked as City Affairs Director for the Associated Students of the University of California at Berkeley. He was elected to the Berkeley Rent Stabilization Board in 2004 and chaired it from 2004 to 2008, and also served on Berkeley's Housing Advisory Commission, Zoning Adjustments Board, and Downtown Area Plan Advisory Committee. (Source: Wikipedia biography.)

He served on the Berkeley City Council representing District 4 from December 2008 to December 1, 2016, over two terms, where he says he drafted or passed more than 300 pieces of legislation, including a $15 local minimum wage, the Downtown Area Plan, an Affordable Housing Mitigation Fee, and police-reform measures. He was elected Mayor of Berkeley in November 2016, took office December 1, 2016, and was re-elected in 2020 with 63% of the vote; Ballotpedia and Wikipedia both describe him as the first Latino, and youngest person in a century, elected to that office. He left the mayor's office December 2, 2024 to take his Senate seat, succeeded as mayor by Adena Ishii. As mayor, the official Senate biography states he 'passed a housing bond and oversaw zoning reforms that resulted in the largest housing construction boom Berkeley had seen in decades,' producing roughly 1,000 affordable units, reduced unsheltered homelessness by 45% through rehousing efforts, strengthened sanctuary-city policies, and authored police-oversight legislation. (Sources: official Senate biography, sd07.senate.ca.gov/biography; Wikipedia biography.)

Arreguín was elected to the State Senate in the November 5, 2024 general election, defeating fellow Democrat Jovanka Beckles (an AC Transit Board member and former Richmond city councilmember) 57.2% to 42.8% (199,423 to 149,415 votes) in this Democratic-hold seat. He was sworn in December 3, 2024. His 2024 campaign was endorsed by the California Democratic Party, United Farm Workers, Planned Parenthood, Gov. Gavin Newsom, and outgoing Sen. Nancy Skinner. (Source: Wikipedia, '2024 California State Senate election,' District 7 results and endorsements section, used because Ballotpedia's page could not be retrieved; see sources note.)

In the Senate, Arreguín chairs the Housing Committee and the Public Safety Committee and has focused legislatively on housing production, tenant and worker protections, police oversight, and Bay Area transit funding, including as a lead coauthor of SB 63 (2025), the Connect Bay Area Act, which placed the five-county Measure RTM transit tax on the November 2026 ballot (see content/measures/scc-measure-rtm-2026.json for the measure itself), and as a coauthor of SB 42 (2025), the California Fair Elections Act of 2026, which placed Proposition 4 on the same ballot (see content/measures/ca-prop-4-2026.json). (Sources: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov bill status pages for SB 63 and SB 42.)

Member, Senate Energy, Utilities and Communications Committee
voting_record_highlights: SB 9 (2025 to 2026), removing the requirement that a property owner reside on-site to build and rent out an accessory dwelling unit: Arreguín was the lead author, with Sen. Jerry McNerney as coauthor. The Assembly concurrence vote passed 31 to 3 on September 3, 2025, and it was signed by the Governor and chaptered October 10, 2025 as Chapter 510, Statutes of 2025. (Source: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov bill status for SB 9, 2025 to 2026.)

SB 63 (2025 to 2026), the Connect Bay Area Act, creating the five-county Public Transit Revenue Measure District and authorizing the ballot measure that became Measure RTM on the November 2026 ballot: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov's bill-status page lists Arreguín alongside Sen. Scott Wiener as one of two lead Senate authors on this bill. That is a different, more senior role than the 'Co-author of SB 63 (2025)' credit line used in content/measures/scc-measure-rtm-2026.json's authors list, which this profile flags rather than silently reconciling. The Senate concurred in Assembly amendments 29 to 8 on September 13, 2025, and it was signed and chaptered October 13, 2025 as Chapter 740, Statutes of 2025. Full analysis of the resulting measure is in content/measures/scc-measure-rtm-2026.json and is not duplicated here. (Source: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov bill status for SB 63, 2025 to 2026.)

SB 42 (2025 to 2026), the California Fair Elections Act of 2026, narrowing the 1988 ban on public financing of candidate campaigns and placing the change before voters as Proposition 4 on the November 2026 ballot: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov lists Arreguín as a coauthor (not a lead author, since Umberg, Allen, and Cervantes hold that role). The Senate concurred in Assembly amendments 29 to 8 on September 13, 2025, and Gov. Newsom signed it October 2, 2025 as Chapter 245, Statutes of 2025. Full analysis of the resulting measure is in content/measures/ca-prop-4-2026.json and is not duplicated here. (Source: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov bill status for SB 42, 2025 to 2026.)
attendance: No individually published floor-attendance or voting-participation record for Senator Arreguín was found. The California State Senate does not publish a per-member attendance scorecard; the only public records are bill-by-bill roll-call votes at leginfo.legislature.ca.gov, which is what the voting-record entries above are drawn from.
